utterances.text: It's your submission on it. You received the documents from the Prosecution, so what are is your submissions on it? Because the objection was recorded for all the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So do you have any submissions to make having received the documents that the Prosecution served?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Our position is very simply we maintain the objection to the admissibility and the authenticity. We have inspected, all the Defence counsel have inspected the one version or the one document which has the 100 in the top corner. We have all inspected that, and our position is that the Prosecution must bring a witness to authenticate this document as -- I know there's been some confusion over these documents because there were several different versions floating around, and it is our understanding based on my lengthy conversation with Ms. Reidy that the one document we're dealing with right now is the one that has the 100 in it, okay? So our position is that they haven't authenticated it. It's not admissible at this point, so the Prosecution needs to bring the witness, who will be subject to cross-examination for purposes of authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. They gave you the statement of the witnesses, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Bernard O'Donnell. Yes, ma'am. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So your position is that you would like to cross-examine that witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Our position is that any document of this sort, they have to bring a witness to sponsor it or show the source of it when there's a question as to authenticity or reliability of the document. So with respect to the one that's in this statement from Bernard O'Donnell, he needs to come testify about the source, which is what Judge Singh had mentioned. If they want to get these documents in, then have the witness who actually got the document tell us where they got the document because this statement doesn't even say where he got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So your position is that the statement you were given is not satisfactory.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's our simple objection, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you would like this maker of the statement to be brought in for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Certainly cross-examination but also -- well, yes. Our position is they need to present this witness to say exactly where it comes from but cross-examination, yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Anything else? Is it your intention that after cross-examination, which ever way the cross-examination goes, do you have witnesses you intend to present just on this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We have no idea because we don't have the full information from this witness. We have a summary here. We don't even know in the full chain of custody, we don't even know who the witnesses are. In his statement, Mr. O'Donnell says that he can talk to the Chamber or tell the Chamber about the witnesses in the chain of custody but at this point, we don't even know who they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So my answer to your question, very simply, is we don't know, Your Honour, if we are going to have witnesses or not because we haven't heard the full testimony of this witness who supposedly is going to authenticate this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Usually -- it depends on your instructions. Usually you would have a position. Maybe you would have had information or instructions from your clients about the document. utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. There being no other matters, the Trial Chamber has one matter dealing with the sitting of the accused in Court each day. We received a report yesterday about the discussions or instructions - I'm not sure which one - which Mr. Pantelic gives the security officers as to how the accused persons should sit in the courtroom each day. So I wanted to find out from Mr. Pantelic whether he has been speaking to the security officers about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As far as I remember, I was of the opinion, according to the instruction of this Trial Chamber at the beginning of the trial, that the position of the defendants during the examination of one witness should be the same during all these days of examination. And having that fact in mind, which for me was absolutely logic - because otherwise, nobody of us can take care about the position if it will be swapped or changed every day - I raised that issue before the responsible officer, and he said that he is in charge of the position of the defendants, not Defence, nor the Registry. And then I was obliged, although I gave all of my excuses to this Trial Chamber, I was obliged to raise that issue and to seek -- to respectfully ask for the instructions with that regard. And I suppose that finally we have the precise situation with that respect, which means that for each next witness, the position of the defendants should be changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Now, yesterday -- because we've heard the last witness for a few days now, yesterday you talked to the security officer about it, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, that was because the new duty officer was not aware about the position of the Trial Chamber, so I just told him to follow these instructions. Yes, that's correct. Yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Now, the position is this: These security officers have got their superior, from whom they receive instructions on who sits where, all right? No Defence counsel has authority to interfere with that, all right? Even if a Defence counsel notices that the sitting is different, all you do is wait for the proceedings to start and raise it with the Chamber. From now on, no Defence counsel will talk to a security officer about the way the accused persons should sit. That is their area of concern. If there is any problem, any Defence counsel should raise it with the Trial Chamber and not with a security officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The security officers do get instructions on a daily basis, or whatever regular times they do, and they're the ones who receive information about security. So if they make any changes of their own accord, or at any time, at any stage, that must be respected. The complaint of any Defence counsel should be directed to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I am absolutely aware of that, and that was case. I addressed that issue to Ms. Registrar, and I didn't make any direct conversation. And then Ms. Registrar told me where -- "Could you tell us what is the situation with regard to the Trial Chamber's instructions?" So I was very well aware of that, and then that was my idea, and I have my colleagues around me that can confirm this situation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- that I immediately addressed this issue to Ms. Registrar. So that was the case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Next time, address the issue to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Wherever the accused sit, it's not a matter for any Defence counsel; it's a matter for the security people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And let's stop this exchange about this problem. The other point is: This Trial Chamber has given instructions, which are standing instructions, that the witnesses must be seated in Court before the Judges enter the courtroom, and these instructions must be complied with. When the accused are brought into the courtroom, they are placed in their place by the security officers. They are supposed to know that they're in the courtroom. When the Defence counsels sit in the courtroom, as well as the Prosecution counsel sit in the courtroom, they know that they're in the courtroom and that before the Judges enter the courtroom, the proceedings are not on. So nobody should speak to the witness, and the witness -- the Prosecution, when they proof their witnesses, they must always give these instructions. This is not a free forum; this is a courtroom. It is very important that we maintain high standards of professionalism, high standards of civilisation, when we are with dealing with these proceedings. When a witness comes in here, she is not on a free forum for anybody to talk to: the Defence counsel, the accused, and anybody else in Court. Can we call the next witness? MR. DI FAZIO: There is, if Your Honours please, the matter of the protection orders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- that I'm seeking. May I make my submissions now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. My submissions will be very brief. I'm seeking facial distortion, a voice distortion, and the attribution of a pseudonym. In making these submissions, can I rely on the -- to a large extent on the motion that was provided and filed with the Chamber on the 14th of November this year and which related to the two previous witnesses who have given evidence. By that, I mean the legal aspects of that motion, the law that is discussed in that motion and the general factual issue relating to the dangers of -- faced by witnesses in the -- in Bosnia these days. All of those matters in that particular motion, that sort of matter, I submit, are pertinent to the -- to this particular witness and so I adopt those. With respect to the factual matter, as far as this witness is concerned, there are really two areas that are causing this witness concern. He lives in a town in Bosnia outside of the Republika Srpska. He has a job as a driver. He drives throughout the northern part of Bosnia as a driver. He drives a small van, that's his job now. He, in the course of carrying out his duties, he has to drive through portions of the Republika Srpska and is worried that when he does that, if it is known that he has provided evidence to the Tribunal, that he might be subject to harassment and threats. His job takes him to Brkco, to Doboj and through, on occasions, to Tuzla. That's the general issue that arises in respect of his work. Insofar as his residence is concerned, there are no concerns as to where he is currently residing but he instructs me that that situation is going to change, he hopes, in the not too distant future. He says that he got his flat back in Bosanski Samac in May of this year, his original flat, the flat he used to live in or apartment he used to live in back in 1992. He says that he's been there, to Bosanski Samac, and that he's cleaned his flat. He's visited it, and that he's prepared it for renovation works. His plans are to go and live in that apartment with his family. He wasn't able to tell me precisely when that happens, when he will do that, but the renovation works he plans for the spring, so presumably sometime the first quarter of next year, I suppose. He instructs me that there have been no threats uttered to him so far, just generally, not because of his status as a witness but just generally in Bosanski Samac, but that he has had the windows to his apartment broken. I asked him if that was a burglary, the result of a burglary or something like that that might explain it, but he was unable to say it was as a result of a burglary. There was nothing to steal, the apartment was empty. He surmises that it was an attack based on ethnic disharmony. So because of those two concerns, he asks me to seek the orders that I do from the Chamber. So in summary, that's the basis of the application, two areas of danger that he's concerned about: his work driving through the Republika Srpska and secondly, the future, his plans to go back, renovate his apartment and move into it with his family, go back to Bosanski Samac, in effect. He's a man with quite a distinctive face. There will be no Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. mistaking him. Once seen, he's the sort of gentleman that anyone would be able to remember, so that's the essence of the Prosecution's submission. I remind the Chamber that in our motion, we pointed out that the Defence would be in no way hamstrung or prejudiced or have their job made in any respect more difficult if those orders were to be granted. They've had full information about this particular witness, and for those reasons, I submit that the other considerations not relating to the defendant, namely the need for public justice and so on will not be -- and the need for the Defence to be able to conduct their Defence effectively will not be prejudiced if you make those orders. Those are my submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we hear from the Defence what their position is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No objection from any of the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The protective measures are granted as requested, facial distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym. And what pseudonym is the Prosecution proposing? MR. DI FAZIO: Witness M. "M" for Mary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So the witness will be referred to as Witness M. So the witness may be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, Your Honour, now we have a changed position, we have to change position of the defendants, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, they can change positions. Who should sit where? They are waiting, and the security also are waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We agreed that that would be the task of the registrar to arrange that, I mean. It was just a request from the Defence as a principle but we are not going into detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can they just rotate, please. If they can just rotate.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can they just rotate. The security will be responsible for that, just rotate them, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: While they're doing that, we just wanted to inquire who the Prosecution was going to call next because we thought they were bringing Esad Dagovic next week, but then Mr. di Fazio said they're bringing a witness on Monday to proof, and it was our understanding that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. di Fazio, who is the witness? MR. DI FAZIO: I believe it is Mr. Dagovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So you're not going to proof him, he's just coming in town then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the problem of the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: It is, with respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Since we are using the pseudonym, can the name be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No, no, we're talking about somebody different, Your Honour. The witness that came several weeks ago. We're not talking about the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. I thought we are going to listen to Witness M. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, we are. I can assure the Chamber that I will provide my learned colleague with all details of the witness this afternoon, if need be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is there a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May I, Madam President? Obviously, it's misunderstanding. Mr. Esad Dagovic was here during the examination-in-chief, now he's going to be cross-examined. As a matter of principle, we don't think that any contact between him and the Prosecutor office should be allowed so that was my -- that was the issue my learned colleague tried to explain, but I tried to narrow the issue and put it on a simple way. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: The way the issue was raised, it didn't alert me to that. Of course we're not going to speak to the witness if he's giving -- if he's already giving evidence. I've been informed by one of the investigators that he was coming to the Tribunal on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For cross-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: For, I assume, for cross-examination. I hadn't realised at the time that the investigator told me that that was the witness who was required to be back for cross-examination. There will be no contact in any improper way with that witness. I provide that solemn assurance, if that is what is troubling my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Nothing was troubling me. We just thought you were bringing a different witness. I'm sorry for the confusion. No, we have no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness be brought, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness did not have his microphone on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The microphone is on, Mr. Usher, because when he was making his solemn declaration, his microphone was not on. The usher hasn't got his microphone so maybe he doesn't get what the Trial Chamber is trying to say.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the microphone was on, actually. It's a remote control by the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay, all right. If the witness can move closer to the microphone. Yes, Mr. di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Mr. Usher, may I ask you to hand this piece of paper to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, will you please look at this document and look at the details on the right-hand side, and without mentioning it, your name, can you tell us if on the right-hand side you see your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Underneath that, do you see your current -- the town of your current residence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Underneath that is a date and I regret that it's -- the month is in English, but I'll inform you that it's the month of March. Apart from that, can you tell us if that is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Are there copies for the Judges? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, there are. Do you wish me to produce that into evidence, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because it's part of the record. MR. DI FAZIO: I seek to produce it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number and it will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the number is P44 under seal. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, in giving your evidence, would you please, as far as you can remember, desist from mentioning your own name in court. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Just relax, Witness. You are going to be here for a while so you can draw your chair in and make yourself more comfortable and settle in. Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What about on your mother's side? Where does her family come from?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness isn't heard by the interpreters. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, just speak up a little more. Your voice has to be picked up by the microphone and it makes it easier if you speak up a little more so the interpreters can hear you and they can interpret what you say and we can all hear what you say, which is very important, okay? Now, my question was where on your mother's side does her family come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How many children do you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And can you give us their sex and their age, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where did you go to school and where were you educated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Following your high school education, did you go on to do some sort of extra training in a craft or trade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: I learned a craft and started working immediately after high school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What is your trade by profession?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: I am a plumber.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After leaving school, what sort of work did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: I worked for a company as a plumber.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Have you received experience as what I call a domestic plumber, and that is plumbing in people's dwelling homes and also on an industrial level, that is plumbing for factory installations, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Does that mean yes to both, both types of experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you perform any military service while you lived in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And where did you -- where did you do that and in what years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And during your military service, where were you deployed, what sort of military unit or activity did you engage in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: It's the so-called technical service, and I did my job as a plumber.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was that throughout your military experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes. First, you had to go through infantry training, and then after that, I started working as a plumber in the technical or engineering service.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After completing your military service, did you go back to Bosanski Samac to live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I want to ask you about your family situation in April of 1992. Again, I remind you, don't use names of any of your family members. I want to know how old your children were back in April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Without giving us the name of the establishment, if any, did your wife work somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What sort of trade or occupation was she engaged in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber if you have ever been a member of a political party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What party, and when did you join it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M
utterances.text: From year 1972, I was a member of the League of Communists, until 1985.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio, we are in open session, and we are concerned about some of the descriptions of the family and the places of work. Is there -- the next part of your examination-in-chief, do we need to go into private session? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I'm just about to get to a point where I will be asking to go into private session, and I've, I thought, kept my answers -- my questions and tried to make sure that the answers were reasonably general up until this point. I don't think there's anything that should cause any concern thus far, is there, Your Honours? I can't see anything other than the description of trades by the witness that could identify him, and I don't think that should be a matter of concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: The only trouble is sometimes the details can lead to identification, excessive details, so I think perhaps just keep it to the elements of the charge, and then -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Okay. We're certainly getting to a point now where I will need private session, and it's important for the actual facts of the case, so I think, to err on the side of safety, we should now go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: at 5.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday the 3rd day of December, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
